name: The Secret Services of the Cold War
description: The agencies, crises and walls of a secret war: CIA against KGB, MI6 against the Stasi, and the codebreakers and atomic secrets that shaped it.

checkpoints.name: From hot war to cold
checkpoints.note: The Manhattan Project and the codebreakers of Colossus show how wartime secrets carried on into peace, as do the OSS and Venona. In 1947 the CIA was founded, the NSA followed, and Mossad, the Securitate and ISI began work as the blocs formed.

checkpoints.name: Walls and spy planes
checkpoints.note: The KGB took shape, West Germany set up its own service, and the Stasi watched East Germans. A U-2 was shot down in 1960, the Bay of Pigs failed in 1961, and the Berlin Wall went up.

checkpoints.name: Missiles and moles
checkpoints.note: After the Cuban Missile Crisis, the services turned to spy satellites and signals, with MI5, MI6 and GCHQ tracking a Soviet network of agents.

checkpoints.name: The last years
checkpoints.note: The Stasi, the Securitate and the KGB were swept away as the Eastern bloc fell. The Warsaw Pact ended and NATO outlived it.
